title: Photosynthesis and Nutrition
seo_title: Primary 6 Basic Science and Technology: Photosynthesis and Nutrition Worksheets (NERDC)
standard_code: Primary 6 Basic Science and Technology: Living and Non-Living Things
standard_text: Green plants make their own food by photosynthesis using sunlight, water and carbon dioxide, and give off oxygen. People need nutrients in food: carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins and minerals, plus water and fibre. A balanced diet keeps us healthy; poor nutrition causes disease. (summary of the Basic Science and Technology curriculum, Primary 6, theme: Living and Non-Living Things)
meta_desc: Free Primary 6 Basic Science and Technology worksheets (NERDC curriculum, theme: Living and Non-Living Things): photosynthesis, light and leaves, nutrients in food, a balanced diet and healthy food choices. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Plants make food from sunlight, water and carbon dioxide.
key_sub: A balanced diet has all the food groups.
body_html:
How to think about it

In photosynthesis, green leaves use sunlight to turn water and carbon dioxide into food (sugar and starch), and give off oxygen. Animals, including people, depend on this food.

Food gives us nutrients: carbohydrates (maize meal, bread) for energy, proteins (beans, eggs, meat) for growth, fats for stored energy, and vitamins and minerals (fruit and vegetables) for health. Too little protein can cause kwashiorkor. Food is processed (dried, cooked, salted, canned) so that it lasts longer.

Example

Which gas do plants take in for photosynthesis?

We breathe it out.

Answer: carbon dioxide

Example

Which nutrient do beans and eggs mainly give?

Needed for growth

Answer: protein

Common mistakes

  • Thinking plants get food from the soil.
  • Thinking fat should never be eaten.
  • Thinking processed food has no nutrients.

faq.q: Why is drying a way to preserve food?
faq.a: Bacteria and fungi need water to grow, so dry food spoils slowly.
Eating the right amounts from all the food groups, with water and fibre.

items.q: Two identical pandan plants were kept for a week, one in light and one in the dark. Everything else was the same. What was being tested?
c: whether the plant needs oxygen to make food
whether light is needed for a plant to make food
whether the plant can grow flowers
items.e: Only one thing was different between the two plants: light.

items.q: Why are leaves green?
items.e: Chlorophyll gives the green colour.

items.q: At night, which gas does a plant give out?
items.e: There is no light at night, so there is no photosynthesis. The plant still respires and gives out carbon dioxide.

items.q: What does chlorophyll do in a leaf?

items.q: How does water reach the leaves to make food?
c: Roots take it in and the water-carrying tubes carry it up.
It is made in the flowers.
Leaves take it in from the air.
items.e: Water travels from the roots up the stem to the leaves.

items.q: On a sunny afternoon, which gas does a healthy plant give out the most?
items.e: In bright light, photosynthesis is faster than respiration, so the plant gives out oxygen overall.
